:::{#exr-span-practice}
#### Testing whether a vector lies in the span of two others

Whether a target can be written as a [linear combination](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-linear-combination) of a few given vectors
is a question about a [span](#def-span).
Let

$$
\vecf{v}_1 = \sbmat{1 \\ 1 \\ 0},
\qquad
\vecf{v}_2 = \sbmat{0 \\ 1 \\ 1},
\qquad
\vecf{w} = \sbmat{3 \\ 5 \\ 2}.
$$

Is the vector $\vecf{w}$ in $\operatorname{span}\cb{\vecf{v}_1, \vecf{v}_2}$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Look for numbers $c_1$ and $c_2$ with $c_1 \vecf{v}_1 + c_2 \vecf{v}_2 = \vecf{w}$,
one entry at a time.

:::

:::
